body:
> In this case, I think class (and others keywords) should not be considered as keyword, but a string literal.

This should be tracked in a [proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals), but I don't think it's a great thing to do for one reason: syntax highlighting.

Not only this would add significant complexity to Godot's own syntax highlighter to make sure the reserved keywords are *not* highlighted as keywords within a Lua-style dictionary, third-party editors always struggle with this kind of "special case" highlighting. They usually don't bother implementing it at all, if they are even aware of this syntax special casing in the first place.

Considering there are 10+ third-party editors that have GDScript syntax highlighting support, I guarantee you at least one of those will fail to highlight it correctly with no fix in sight. I see this happen a lot with languages that have keywords that are only reserved in certain circumstances.

The effort required to add quotes around the reserved keyword is much lower than having to modify all these syntax highlighters. We can also modify the Dictionary script errors to mention that reserved identifiers need to be quoted to work.

It's fair. But the burden to use quotes in my case it's bigger than having a word with wrong highlight. I'm building a HTML Builder, so class is a very common tag attribute.
```gdscript
b.div(func():
  b.span("Read more")
  b.a("here", {class="btn btn-link", href="example.com", target="_blank"})
)
```
Writing `{"class"="...", foo="..."}` everytime is unwanted. But since my project isn't the main use case for Godot/Gdscript, I can adapt to use something like `cls="..."`, `classes="..."` or `class_name="..."`, it isn't ideal, but it's better than using quotes.

>  I'm building a HTML Builder, so class is a very common tag attribute.

React worked around this issue by having its `class` attribute named `className` (it's converted back to `class` automatically when it builds HTML from JSX). I believe many other web frameworks did something similar, as you said.
